recorded.values: INVENTED. Every Opportunity pair below is synthetic. R1 SL-3's Definition of Done says hosted evidence uses shadow traffic, controlled or pilot-derived as available, and that organically occurring live duplicates are NOT a prerequisite — so this set is built rather than harvested. The shapes are modelled on S1 §8.6 (duplicate), §8.5.3 (continuity uncertainty), AC-15 (conflicting facts) and EC-05 (a substantial criteria change may still be one objective), and on the opening forms S1 §8.4.3 names. No production lead, message, contact or property is reproduced here.
recorded.gap: This set is wholly synthetic, which is a real limitation and is stated rather than hidden: it measures whether the judge follows the approved continuity semantics, not how it behaves on the actual distribution of Alebrixe conversations. Pilot-derived pairs enter the same way SL-2's real openings did — captured under an explicit bounded authorization, redacted, and labelled by human review independently of the model's own output, with `modelSaid` never copied into `expected`.
recorded.barEstablishedBy: PROPOSED AND FROZEN BY THE CODING AGENT on 2026-09-07, BEFORE this set was run even once, per Methodology §14.1 and the SL-3 Definition of Done — not by a human, and with no human approval sought or given at that point. It was not moved after results were observed: the first run breached the false-merge bar and the JUDGE was repaired, leaving both bars and every expected label untouched. RATIFIED BY THE HUMAN ACCOUNTABLE on 2026-09-07, AFTER reviewing the recorded runs — a review of an already-frozen bar, not a prior approval of it. The ratification is limited to SL-3 shadow evidence and establishes no general Relationship Operations, assisted-stage or live-stage quality threshold.

bar_rationale: Two bars, because the two error directions are not equally costly. The Slice's own risk table says a FALSE MERGE is worse than a missed one, since it conflates two real objectives and hands one advisor a responsibility that was never theirs; a missed duplicate merely leaves two Opportunities standing, which is recoverable and which the next determination can fix. So: at most 20% overall failures across the semantic set — looser than SL-2's 15%, because sameness-of-objective is a harder and more contestable judgment than presence-of-objective — and ZERO scenarios labelled distinct may be judged same_objective, including the false_merge_trap cases built specifically to invite the error.

scenarios.note: Two empty openers look identical precisely because neither says anything. Merging them would conflate two unrelated prospects on the strength of no evidence at all — the exact failure the Slice's risk table calls worse than a missed duplicate.

scenarios.label: TRAP — the same generic objective text, no other overlap

recentMessages: Busco casa por el sur, hasta 2 millones
Busco casa en Saltillo, presupuesto amplio, como 6 millones

scenarios.note: Identical summary strings, different city and a triple budget gap. A judge that anchors on the objective label rather than the evidence merges these.

scenarios.label: TRAP — two different prospects asking about the same listing

left.objective: comprar la casa anunciada en Cumbres
recentMessages: ¿Sigue disponible? Somos familia de 4 y vamos con crédito

right.objective: comprar la casa anunciada en Cumbres como inversión
recentMessages: Me interesa como inversión, pagaría de contado para ponerla en renta

scenarios.note: The strongest trap in the set: a shared property context is the signal most likely to be mistaken for a shared objective. Two buyers wanting the same house are two objectives, and merging them would close one real prospect's responsibility under another's.
